items.title: Second federal judge blocks Trump birthright citizenship ban
items.feedTitle: Second judge invalidates Trump's new attempt to restrict birthright citizenship
items.summary: A federal judge in Washington, D.C. issued a preliminary injunction blocking the Trump administration's attempt to restrict birthright citizenship, marking the second court to reject the policy. The judge issued a 67-page opinion asserting protections under the Citizenship Clause. This continues a legal pattern of courts blocking the administration's citizenship restrictions.

items.title: Army confirms successful detonation of Iowa lead azide stockpile
items.feedTitle: All 5 tons of lead azide were successfully destroyed in Iowa detonation, US Army says
items.summary: The U.S. Army reported that all 5 tons of deteriorating lead azide were successfully destroyed in a controlled detonation at an Iowa ammunition plant on Wednesday. Officials said the threat of spontaneous explosions has been eliminated, though monitoring for environmental impact is ongoing. The detonation proceeded despite weeks of public health concerns from residents.

items.title: Inflation remains stubbornly high, despite a drop in gas prices
items.feedTitle: Inflation remains stubbornly high, despite a drop in gas prices
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: Trump administration announces broad new tariffs on trading partners
items.feedTitle: Trump administration to raise tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others
items.summary: The Trump administration unveiled new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, the EU, Brazil and others, citing unfair trade practices and investigations into excess industrial capacity. The levies include a proposed 20% additional tax on Chinese imports, which would bring totals to around 40%. India proposes capping tariffs at 17% if a trade deal is reached.

items.title: Thousands of legal immigrants lose Medicaid coverage under Trump policy
items.feedTitle: Thousands of immigrants with legal status lose Medicaid coverage
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of immigrants living legally in the U.S. have recently lost their Medicaid coverage under provisions of Trump's signature tax and spending law. The law is projected to reduce federal Medicaid spending by $900 billion over the next decade. The loss affects immigrants who meet income and other eligibility requirements but are considered subject to public charge restrictions.

stlouis.title: Winter storm threatens St. Louis Thanksgiving travel with heavy snow
stlouis.feedTitle: First winter weather threat in 265 days targets St. Louis as Thanksgiving travel ramps up
stlouis.summary: St. Louis is under a winter storm watch as forecasters warn of heavy snow potentially arriving Wednesday through Thanksgiving, the first significant winter weather in 265 days. Missouri transportation officials are preparing for possible record snow levels. Multiple advisories and storm warnings have been upgraded as conditions worsen.

stlouis.title: Former St. Louis Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner disbarred
stlouis.feedTitle: Former St. Louis City Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner disbarred
stlouis.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court has disbarred former St. Louis Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner, marking a significant disciplinary action against the high-profile prosecutor. This action comes after prior controversy surrounding her tenure in office.

stlouis.title: St. Louis Blues resilience redefining their season
stlouis.feedTitle: The resilience of the St. Louis Blues is redefining their season
stlouis.summary: The St. Louis Blues' resilience has become a defining characteristic as the team navigates its season, drawing praise from analysts for their ability to bounce back from adversity. The team's performance reflects broader themes of perseverance amid challenges.

items.title: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi refinery and Riyadh tower
items.feedTitle: Middle East latest: Houthis claim attacks on refinery and Riyadh as Saudis strike Hodeidah port
items.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for attacks on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery at Ras Tanura and a tower in Riyadh, saying the strikes were in retaliation for Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah port. The attacks highlight escalating regional tensions and threats to critical infrastructure in the Middle East.

items.title: Colombian police end supermarket siege, free all hostages
items.feedTitle: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket
items.summary: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in Cartagena after a 17-hour siege, rescuing all hostages held during what authorities described as a failed robbery of a cash-laden armored car. One gunman was killed in the operation. The incident highlighted ongoing security concerns in one of Colombia's most popular tourist cities.

items.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
items.feedTitle: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
items.summary: Israeli judges recommended dropping the most serious charges against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases. Netanyahu has called for his trial to end, and the recommendation represents a significant development in the high-profile case.

items.title: Lululemon founder sparks outrage with sexist comments on birthrates
items.feedTitle: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
items.summary: Lululemon founder Chip Wilson drew sharp criticism after suggesting that women in Canada are having too few children, leading some men to bring in brides from Thailand. The remarks at a women's leadership conference stunned attendees and sparked widespread backlash over their misogyny.

items.title: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war, estimate shows
items.feedTitle: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war, new estimate suggests
items.summary: New estimates suggest that more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed since the start of the Ukraine war, based on leaked data that reveals how the conflict has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia. The figure is higher than Russia's own publicly stated losses of nearly 500,000.

items.title: US to cap India tariff at 17% if trade deal is reached
items.feedTitle: US to cap India tariff at 17% if trade deal is reached, USTR says
items.summary: The U.S. Trade Representative said the U.S. will cap tariffs on India at 17% if a trade deal is reached, proposed at 25% otherwise. India has rejected claims that its policies fuel excess manufacturing capacity, saying it has no structural excess capacity in any sector. Early negotiations are underway to reach a bilateral trade agreement.

items.title: Indian Cockroach movement leader stopped from flying to UK
items.feedTitle: Indian Cockroach movement leader asks court for permission to fly to UK
items.summary: Saurav Das, leader of India's youth-led Cockroach movement, was stopped by immigration officials at Delhi airport and asked the high court for permission to fly to the UK. Officials cited a last-minute notice over his passport as the reason for the delay. Das had been invited to speak at British universities.

items.title: India opens prized missile test range to Japan for first time
items.feedTitle: India opens doors to prized missile test range for Japan for first time, hypersonics collaboration on cards
items.summary: India has opened its prized missile test range to Japan for the first time, marking a deepening of strategic military cooperation. The move signals potential collaboration on hypersonics technology and represents significant expansion of India-Japan defense ties amid regional security concerns.

items.title: China-Pakistan satellites monitor India 24/7, report alleges
items.feedTitle: Exclusive: China-Pakistan satellite waltz is watching every inch of India 24×7
items.summary: An exclusive report alleges that Chinese and Pakistani satellites have been conducting around-the-clock surveillance of India, with three Chinese satellites frequently scanning India's western coast. The findings raise national security concerns and have drawn criticism that the government downplayed China's role in recent military operations.

items.title: India wins Visitors' Lion for best national art participation
items.feedTitle: India Wins Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at Venice Art Biennale 2026
items.summary: India received the Visitors' Lion award for best national participation at the Venice Art Biennale 2026, marking recognition of the country's artistic contribution. Prime Minister Modi hailed the win as a proud moment for India's cultural standing on the global stage.

immigration.title: IBM ends green card sponsorship, gives H-1B workers relocation ultimatum
immigration.feedTitle: IBM gives H-1B employees 3 weeks to choose between relocation and job loss
immigration.summary: IBM has announced it is ending green card sponsorships and given H-1B visa employees in its largest division just three weeks to choose between relocating or leaving the company by end of 2026. The move reflects broader industry recalibration of foreign worker programs and represents significant disruption for affected employees.

immigration.title: DOL proposes sweeping overhaul of PERM labor certification program
immigration.feedTitle: DOL Proposes Sweeping Modernization Of The Perm Labor Certification Program
immigration.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor has proposed major changes to the PERM labor certification process, including a 90-day recruitment requirement and a 2-year layoff bar for employers. The proposed rule strengthens standards for protecting U.S. workers and would significantly change how employers sponsor foreign workers for permanent positions. This is proposed, not yet final.

immigration.title: H-1B premium processing fee rises to $2,965 for FY2028
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B premium processing rises to $2,965: Key info for Indian F-1 OPTs for FY2028
immigration.summary: USCIS has raised the H-1B premium processing fee to $2,965 ahead of the FY2028 lottery, increasing costs for Indian F-1 OPT workers seeking expedited visa processing. The fee increase represents a significant cost factor for visa applicants and renewal applicants seeking priority handling.

items.title: US inflation hits 3.8% in October, highest since May
items.feedTitle: US inflation hits highest since May after prices climb 3.8% over the last year
items.summary: The Commerce Department reported consumer prices rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier, the highest reading since May, amid soaring energy prices and persistent cost pressures. The data comes ahead of a crucial Federal Reserve board meeting on rate decisions and signals ongoing inflation concerns that could influence monetary policy.

items.title: Nvidia leads tech sell-off as AI concerns resurface despite Huang's return
items.feedTitle: Nvidia leads tech sell-off as Huang comeback rally fizzles and AI concerns return
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell sharply as the initial relief rally from CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement fizzled and investor concerns over AI valuations and profitability returned. The tech-heavy Nasdaq declined nearly 4% as the broader AI sector faced renewed skepticism about whether the hype justifies current valuations.

items.title: Indian markets surge 1.8% on foreign fund inflows and crude decline
items.feedTitle: Sensex, Nifty surge nearly 2% to post their best session since November 6
items.summary: The Sensex jumped 1,502 points and Nifty surged to 25,819 as foreign institutional investors returned to Indian markets and crude oil prices declined. The rally marked the best session since November 6, with banking and consumer stocks leading gains. Markets have now recouped nearly all 2026 losses through November gains.

items.title: Stocks slump as investors fret over AI, tariffs, and inflation
items.feedTitle: Stocks Slump Again as Investors Fret About A.I., Tariffs and Inflation
items.summary: U.S. stock markets declined amid investor concerns over artificial intelligence valuations, new Trump tariffs on 14 trading partners, and persistent inflation pressures. The sell-off reflected heightened uncertainty about the AI sector's sustainability and broader trade policy impacts on corporate earnings.

items.title: SpaceX wins FCC approval for 1 million Starmind data center satellites
items.feedTitle: SpaceX wins FCC approval to deploy 1 million orbital data center satellites
items.summary: Federal regulators approved SpaceX's plan to deploy 1 million orbital data center satellites under the Starmind project, with 100,000 satellites to be deployed by November 2035. The approval signals support for private-sector space infrastructure development and Elon Musk hailed it as a significant asset for America and the world.

cards.title: Control the Controllable
cards.insight: Stoic wisdom teaches that we possess direct control only over our judgments, intentions, and responses—not over external outcomes or others' actions. In markets and policy, distinguishing between what we can influence and what we cannot prevents wasted energy and poor decisions.
cards.takeaway: When facing tariffs, rate decisions, or stock volatility, focus energy on decisions within your control—portfolio rebalancing, risk management, preparation—rather than on predicting or resenting external forces.

cards.title: Virtue Over Profit
cards.insight: Marcus Aurelius and Epictetus reminded us that virtue—acting with integrity, wisdom, and justice—is the highest good, not wealth or status. A person of principle endures market cycles and policy shifts with composure because their worth isn't tied to portfolio performance.
cards.takeaway: Build financial and professional choices on principles of fairness and long-term integrity, not short-term gain. This foundation proves more resilient than reactive trading or ethical shortcuts.

cards.title: Amor Fati: Love Your Fate
cards.insight: Stoics cultivated the practice of embracing unavoidable circumstances rather than resisting them. Market downturns, inflation spikes, and policy changes are facts; wisdom lies in adapting resourcefully rather than complaining about injustice.
cards.takeaway: When confronted with tariffs, rate hikes, or geopolitical risk, ask: 'How can I thrive within this new reality?' rather than 'Why is this happening to me?'

cards.title: Memento Mori: Remember Mortality
cards.insight: Stoics used the awareness of life's brevity to strip away superficial concerns. Remembering that wealth, status, and even markets are temporary focuses the mind on what truly matters—meaningful work, relationships, and character.
cards.takeaway: Let awareness of time's limits guide you toward decisions that build lasting value—skills, relationships, reputation—rather than chasing fleeting gains or reacting to noise.

ai.title: Anthropic CEO denies surrendering human control to AI systems
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
ai.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushed back against accusations that the company is ceding control to AI systems, calling such claims 'absurd.' He reiterated that humans retain decision-making authority over AI systems. The comments come amid broader debates about AI autonomy and safety in the tech industry.

ai.title: California sues OpenAI over alleged unsafe AI development practices
ai.feedTitle: California sues OpenAI over alleged unsafe AI development practices
ai.summary: California has sued OpenAI alleging unsafe AI development practices, raising regulatory concerns about how leading AI companies operate. The lawsuit reflects growing state-level scrutiny of AI safety standards and corporate governance in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence sector.

ai.title: Explainer: How China accessed Nvidia AI chips despite U.S. export bans
ai.feedTitle: EXPLAINER: How China got access to Nvidia's AI chips despite rules to stop them
ai.summary: An explainer examines how Chinese entities obtained Nvidia's advanced AI chips despite U.S. export control rules designed to restrict access. The findings raise questions about enforcement of technology restrictions and security implications of potential loopholes in export control systems.

ai.title: Chinese AI firms face severe delays as U.S. tightens chip access
ai.feedTitle: Chinese AI Model Development Faces Severe Delays, Widening Gap With US - The Information
ai.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence companies confront a dire future as the United States tightens restrictions on chip access and AI tokens, widening the competitive gap with U.S. AI developers. The constraints threaten to slow Chinese AI model development significantly compared to progress in the United States.

ai.title: Former OpenAI CTO's startup releases Inkling 2 Mini offline AI model
ai.feedTitle: The startup of the former CTO of OpenAI has released Inkling 2 Mini — an AI model for programming without the Internet. It needs about 20 GB of memory to run.
ai.summary: A startup founded by a former OpenAI CTO has released Inkling 2 Mini, an AI model for programming that runs offline and requires approximately 20 GB of memory. The release offers developers a locally-deployed alternative to cloud-based AI programming tools.
